    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Sources indicate that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Sources indicate that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's key to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    Industry observers note that we already know the Wild are major-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    Recent findings suggest that it was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    According to recent reports, similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    #15805. Breaking: Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1181 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec.
    • In a recent development, the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No.
    • "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

    In a recent development, the decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He highlighted few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Industry observers note that will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" ….

    Industry observers note that the Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the massive-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

    According to recent reports, coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

    Recent findings suggest that the Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

    According to recent reports, the Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

    Eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.

    Industry observers note that while Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench.

    In a recent development, that 25-point performance represents a fresh season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently.

    "Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason mentioned.

    Tari Eason on what allowed him to have a season-high 25 points off the bench tonight:"Shit, the Wizards, for real." pic.twitter.com/t4bOwtzw5r.

    In a recent development, A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that the Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.

    Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    In a recent development, emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Recent findings suggest that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    In a recent development, emery remarked: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    “Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    Sources indicate that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    It has been revealed that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    Sources indicate that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a massive chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    In a recent development, villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

    It has been revealed that after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    According to recent reports, both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

    Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

    Recent findings suggest that 💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

    Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season.

    PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

    Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

    Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

    Sources indicate that not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    Industry observers note that one final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

    Recent findings suggest that alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    Sources indicate that aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a substantial chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    Sources indicate that doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

    Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days?     Industry observers note that what will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    In a recent development, unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    According to recent reports, the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    Recent findings suggest that “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    In a recent development, “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    #15800. How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1403 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1403 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • Let's take a look at four major reasons.
    • According to recent reports, giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    How have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    According to recent reports, giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    Recent findings suggest that as pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the big who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    Recent findings suggest that the soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    These are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    They are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a massive step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    In a recent development, that is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    Mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    It has been revealed that the Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    According to recent reports, of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    Sources indicate that then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    Industry observers note that thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a fresh home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    In a recent development, over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been massive in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    Miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    Through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    Translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    Recent findings suggest that cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    All of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.

    The QB ranking here is handled by Garrett Podell, who breaks down every possible QB stat to figure out who should be on top, and since Burrow leads the NFL in nearly every conceivable stat, it was an easy decision.

    Here's a short explanation from Garrett of how his QB ranking works: "These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season." By the time the game kicked off, the 49ers were fully acclimated to the 17-hour time difference, and it showed: San Francisco won 27-7.

The core of this team is one of the oldest in the NHL, and not even Sidney Crosby can remain an elite superstar forever.

    If the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When the Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City this week, they'll face multiple challenges, including one they've never really dealt with: altitude.

    In a recent development, the Vikings' showdown with the 49ers on Sunday night will take place at Estadio Azteca, which sits at an elevation of just over 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, that's more than 2,000 feet higher than the altitude in Denver, which has the highest elevation of any NFL city at 5,280 feet.

    To get acclimated to the altitude, the 49ers are spending their week of practice in Colorado Springs, where the elevation is over 6,600 feet. On the Vikings' end, they've spent the week at their normal practice facility, but they do have a secret weapon that will help them acclimate to the high elevation: The team has been using what is essentially an altitude chamber for the past few weeks.

    Rather than leaving Minnesota to train at altitude before Sunday night’s game in Mexico City, the Vikings built an altitude chamber in Eagan, where players can get familiar with the effects of working in thinner air before Sunday’s game at 7,200 feet (photos courtesy of the… pic.twitter.com/b9FWMF3KxJ.

    In a recent development, the room is full of exercise equipment — like stationary bikes and treadmills — and it lets players simulate training at altitudes up to 12,000 feet. So while they aren't fully practicing in those conditions, they are working out and, they hope, slowly getting their bodies ready.

    The Vikings did give some thought to relocating for the week, but in the end, the team didn't want to take the players out of their normal routine, according to Vikings Vice President of Player Health and Performance, Tyler Williams.

    "As much as they enjoy prime-time games, they love that Sunday-to-Sunday weekly rhythm, and there's so many things now that players take in on nutrition and body work and all their recovery processes and what they do to prepare," Williams remarked, via the Vikings official website. "They like their Mondays being their Mondays. We're rhythm-and-process-habit people. And so, knowing that we can reduce [those variables] by staying here, that went into the equation.".

    When you're at a higher elevation, each breath takes in fewer oxygen molecules, which is why athletes get winded faster when playing at these altitudes. That science is why the Vikings felt the addition of the chamber was necessary.

    "A couple things that [it] looks to achieve: Even though you're not doing a full practice at altitude, you're trying to gain a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams remarked.

    Was fascinating to hear #Vikings VP of health & performance Tyler Williams speak about preparing the team for Sunday's game in Mexico City at an altitude of 7,352 feet. Process includes this temporary altitude room at TCO. Players have spent time in there going back many weeks. pic.twitter.com/9t12eM5l1d.

    The Vikings installed the chamber more than five weeks ago, and since then, the players have been taking advantage of it in the facility.

    It has been revealed that "I'd say to date, we have close to 450 sessions accumulated in there," Williams mentioned. "Nearly our whole roster has done five-plus sessions and nearly our whole roster has [experienced] 12,000 feet, which is great.".

    The team's goal is simple: The Vikings want every player on the roster to be at least somewhat acclimated to the altitude once they land in Mexico City.

    Industry observers note that "The more often you're exposed to that, you have a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams said. "You also have a behavioral adaptation — how your body responds to [altitude]; how you know how to pace yourself at altitude; how you know how to breathe and use breathing strategies in your first exposure compared to your fifth is totally different. It's a learned adaptation.".

    If you're wondering whether the players like the chamber, the answer seems to be yes, at least according to Justin Jefferson.

    According to recent reports, "It's been really good," Jefferson stated of the chamber this week. "It's good to have that feel and to kind of get acclimated to that feeling of being in that altitude. For the past four or five weeks we've been training in there, trying to get our lungs acclimated to taking that. It's different for sure. It's different than what we're really used to, but I feel like we're ready, and they got us well prepared to play fast and play freely and not really [be] thinking about all the extra stuff that goes into it.

    Although this should help the Vikings, they won't be quite as acclimated as San Francisco. With the 49ers spending the week in Colorado, they'll be eating, sleeping and practicing at the higher altitude 24 hours a day, which should fully acclimate their body. On the other hand, the Vikings are only using the chamber for workouts — they're not practicing in it — so it's not quite the same as being fully immersed in a higher altitude like the 49ers.

    It has been revealed that according to scientific research, it generally takes one to three days to fully adjust to a higher altitude, but the Vikings won't have that time since they'll be arriving in Mexico City on Saturday. The Vikings are clearly hoping that the altitude chamber will help them adjust just enough to pull out a win in this huge NFC showdown.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was sent home by the team on Thursday and will not be active when the Ravens take on the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte this Sunday, head coach Jesse Minter told reporters.

    Minter said this is just a one-game deactivation, and that the conversations they are having are "very personal and private," and "need to remain that [way] for the good of the team and the organization.".

    Industry observers note that "This is a team thing, in my opinion. With what's transpired, and look, he's going to be dealing with this a lot more probably than the rest of the team ... This is about the team and putting us in the best position to be successful...".

    Coach Minter on Marlon Humphrey pic.twitter.com/zI2xoYoOfD.

    Humphrey found himself in hot water after saying that the city of Baltimore is best at making "criminals" during a recent taping of his podcast.

    "What is Baltimore best at making? They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said on "The Marlon Humphrey Show" Tuesday. He then added, "Yeah, no, that's obviously going to get cut out.".

    Humphrey attempted to retract his insult to the city of Baltimore on Wednesday.

    It has been revealed that "I apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey stated Wednesday, via The Baltimore Sun. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. I've spent a lot of offseasons here, welcomed a son here, and I'm an investor in the city, investor in different parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and I'd just like to apologize for those comments.".

    Despite Humphrey's apology, this had already become a major story. Even Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott issued a scathing statement on the matter.

    "While we acknowledge Marlon's apology, a verbal apology is not enough," Scott mentioned in a statement, via The Baltimore Sun, on Wednesday. "Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper. I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs, but we have recently lost our way.

    It has been revealed that "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world. I invite Marlon to sit down with me and some Baltimoreans who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made.".

    Recent findings suggest that humphrey has recorded 40 tackles, nine passes defensed and two forced fumbles in 10 games played this season. The 30-year-old corner is in the final season of a five-year, $97.5 million contract and his $26.3 million cap hit in 2026 leads all NFL cornerbacks, according to Over The Cap.

    It has been revealed that humphrey is a four-time Pro Bowler and two-time First Team All-Pro, but as pointed out by Mayor Scott, his play has dipped. Humphrey's 507 yards allowed in man coverage are the fourth-most in the NFL, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. This season, he is allowing a career-high 9.5 yards per target and the second-highest passer rating against in his 10-year career, at 94.4, per Next Gen Stats.

    In Humphrey's place this week, Minter said Chidobe Awuzie and TJ Tampa will see an increase in their snap counts.

    "He's very remorseful. I think he really understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city, and when you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate," Minter said on Thursday.

    In a recent development, this season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    That's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He right now has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    In a recent development, during the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    In a recent development, with the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    Boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Industry observers note that acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    It has been revealed that the Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are right now riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    #15788. Latest Update: Revisiting the Chiefs' 2026 NFL Draft: Was Kansas City justified in trading up for Mansoor Delane?

    Latest Update: Revisiting the Chiefs' 2026 NFL Draft: Was Kansas City justified in trading up for Mansoor Delane?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Kansas City Chiefs made significant changes to their offense by moving on from offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and spending substantial on running back Kenneth Walker III, but the sheer volume of moves on defense was more impressive.
    • In a recent development, the Chiefs were flush with draft capital after trading cornerback Trent McDuffie to Los Angeles.
    • In a recent development, kansas City traded away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and allowed cornerback Jaylen Watson to walk in free agency.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Kansas City Chiefs made significant changes to their offense by moving on from offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and spending substantial on running back Kenneth Walker III, but the sheer volume of moves on defense was more impressive. On the heels of an uncharacteristic 6-11 season, the franchise bid farewell to a trio of defensive starters and even more depth.

    In a recent development, the Chiefs were flush with draft capital after trading cornerback Trent McDuffie to Los Angeles. The team utilized its newfound wealth to revamp the defense. How are those decisions maturing halfway through the regular season?

    In a recent development, kansas City traded away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and allowed cornerback Jaylen Watson to walk in free agency. Leadership decided to reallocate financial resources elsewhere and invest in the position through the draft. After acquiring Nohl Williams in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, the Chiefs traded up from No. 9 overall to No. 6 overall, in exchange for third- and fifth-round picks, for the right to select Delane.

    When available, Delane has been excellent. He operates with supreme awareness of his surroundings and plays aggressively downhill in run support. The LSU product is not afraid to be physical at the line of scrimmage or through the route. He has the top-end speed to stay in-phase when covering crossing routes, but has been known to allow receivers behind him.

    According to recent reports, delane has missed three games this season due to injury. TruMedia credits him with 234 yards and 1 touchdown allowed on 15 receptions.

    According to recent reports, if the Chiefs hadn't traded up, would another team have picked him sooner? Teams generally have an inkling of another team's interest when making such a move. The Commanders and Saints sat ahead of Kansas City before the trade. Odds are good Washington would have taken Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles Jr., but the Saints were the real mystery. New Orleans lost Alontae Taylor in free agency and Kool-Aid McKinstry's play had been frustrating, to say the least. They ultimately selected Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson before signing veteran cornerback Martin Emerson shortly after the draft.

    Although it was a relatively steep price to pay for a cornerback, Kansas City was convinced about the player and thought he might no longer be available if they waited; the reasoning was sound. Those resources could have helped address the team's wide receiver problem. Notre Dame's Malachi Fields was literally taken with the third-round pick Cleveland received, and Caleb Douglas was taken one pick later.

    Kansas City would then select Clemson defensive tackle Peter Woods at 29th overall. Defensive tackle is a position the Chiefs had been linked to throughout the pre-draft process, so it did not come as a surprise when they elected to address it. Were they too rigid in their approach rather than adapting as the first round progressed?

    As established quarterbacks advance into the latter stages of their careers, teams often prioritize other roster needs rather than helping them. Green Bay's track record of not drafting wide receivers in the first round ran parallel to Aaron Rodgers' career, for example. Any offensive deficiency can be masked by Patrick Mahomes' performance or Andy Reid's play-calling; that is how the franchise has operated.

    Until this off-season's signing of Walker, notable skill position changes included the trade of Tyreek Hill and the signings of Hollywood Brown or DeAndre Hopkins. Neither was a particular needle-mover.

    It has been revealed that if the Chiefs had been more open-minded, would Washington wide receiver Denzel Boston or Indiana wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. have impacted this year's team more? Hindsight is 20-20, but it would be difficult to debate that argument.

    Among 31 rookies with 50+ pass-rushing snaps this season, Woods ranks second-to-last in pressure rate (2.2%), according to TruMedia. He also has not been credited with a defensive run stuff.

    Delane looks like a high-quality long-term starter. Cornerback is an incredibly volatile position year-over-year, and only a small number can maintain a level of excellence in the NFL. Too often, people see a high number of interceptions and equate that to coverage ability; some of the worst contracts in the league have been doled out as a result of that flawed way of thinking.

    The conversation is particularly interesting regarding Kansas City because the franchise has traded away Marcus Peters, L'Jarius Sneed and McDuffie over the years. Will Delane spend his entire career with the Chiefs or become a trade chip down the road?

    Regarding Woods, he does not turn 22 until March, so it is too early to definitively say what his career will look like. However, he has yet to prove how he will win as a pass rusher in the NFL, and his run defense has hardly been better. The players who initially struggle to contribute rarely develop into difference-makers.

    If Woods eventually occupies the role Chris Jones has held for a decade, the team may salvage value, but early returns have been disappointing.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    According to recent reports, after a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    According to recent reports, james, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    Recent findings suggest that what's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    The annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    According to recent reports, otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings.

    Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.

    Recent findings suggest that now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

    It has been revealed that the Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around.".

    According to recent reports, crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.

    It has been revealed that the Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the Newly introduced York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.

    The pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.

    According to recent reports, we ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- currently remain under contract/team control.

    According to recent reports, the AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and Latest York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.

    It is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps Fresh York would pounce.

    It has been revealed that teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is stated to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.

    Industry observers note that ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.

    Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
    • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
    • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

    There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

    Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

    You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

    It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes indicated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

    Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

    Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

    Sources indicate that the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward promptly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

    The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

    It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

    It has been revealed that devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

    Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

    There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

    It has been revealed that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

    Sources indicate that top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

    Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

    He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

    It has been revealed that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

    Sources indicate that it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

    This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Upcoming Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

    While Leeds will have upcoming signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.
